endorsements.name: Tim Helming
endorsements.label: Domain Blooms: Do Adversaries Leverage the Zeitgeist to Do Bad Things?
endorsements.description: When in the course of (information-age) human events large things happen, they inevitably have online echoes. Meanwhile, we know that every domain on the Internet has a job to do, and in many cases, that job is to trick a human into doing something against their own self-interest. When ideas become prominent in the zeitgeist—that is, they’re on a lot of people’s minds—domains are registered with the idea of leveraging folks’ attention. From an infosec perspective, we sought to learn more about the aggregate risk profile of domains whose names included major societal themes (such as COVID-19, Black Lives Matter, Ukraine, etc) to see whether these domains carried more risk than the ongoing “background noise” on the Internet. Spoiler alert: some of them do. This talk describes domain blooms and a related pattern we call “spikes,” and the relative risks of phishing, malware, and spam associated with these patterns.
